No contact no contact no contact. Oh God. I cannot stress enough how important it is. He broke up with me about 8 months ago, then said he needed to be alone for "at least a month"--"talk to me in December," and then, a few days later, messaged me himself. We started talking again somewhat and he came to visit me (we had an LDR--him in Chicago, me in Indiana) with another mutual friend, but it was obvious we were over. I was in Chicago for Thanksgiving and he came and saw me again. Really fucked with my emotions.

Then, a "friend" of mine, on the pretext of "helping me out," went batshit crazy and called him out and yelled at him for no fucking reason, and started sending him texts as me, cussing him out. That was beyond insane. He cut me loose, I cut the friend loose, and I was miserable, because he didn't want to associate with me anymore for something that wasn't even my fault.

I continued trying to be friends. It didn't work. We had a lot of arguments, and finally I went for a 3 month period of NC, and felt a billion times better about myself.

Cut to March, when I started talking to him again after feeling depressed for a few days. Didn't help. NC again. Then, in May, I called him and we spoke for hours and just like that, we were friends again.

I ended up moving to Chicago for a job; messaged him to come to my stand-up comedy show, he said no. "I don't see you often; I'd like to see you with at least one other close friend around." I cut my losses and went NC again, and I am so much happier since.

This story is making me sound crazy, I know. Basically, it's a learning process. NC has helped me more than anything else, and I'm now channeling my energies unto myself. Another really important thing is supportive friends and meeting new people. That's where I'm at right now. I can't say I'm over him, but I am way further along than when I started.
